audience: Anyone who quotes jobs by the hour
series: Flagship #23 (SALES FIRST); week of Oct 12 theme day 2; reframes the Oct 11 trade hook into the broad H02 'looks fine, break-even is' frame that drew 98 views in a day on #22 (Oct 12 pm); CMO slate Oct 13 am
hook: $25 an hour looks fine. Break-even is $62.36
hook_say: Your pay over all your hours looks like $25 an hour. Count unpaid hours, tax and costs, and break-even is $62.36.

rows.label: Take-home pay you want
rows.say: You want to take home $60,000 a year
rows.why: The calculator's example: $60,000 a year of take-home pay.

rows.label: Hours you work (48 wks x 50)
rows.why: 48 weeks of 50 hours, counting quoting, driving and admin.

rows.label: Pay over all your hours
rows.why: $60,000 divided by 2,400 hours. This is the usual guess.

rows.label: Hours customers pay for (60%)
rows.say: Customers pay for only 1,440 of them
rows.why: 60% of 2,400 hours. The rest is driving, quotes and admin.

rows.label: Tax + business costs
rows.why: About $21,223 of self-employment and income tax plus $8,580 of yearly costs ($715 a month).

rows.label: Break-even per paid hour
rows.why: $89,803 of revenue needed over 1,440 paid hours.

fix.label: Rate where 15% of the price is profit
fix.say: Price it so 15% of each dollar is profit: $73.37 an hour
fix.why: Break-even divided by 0.85, so 15% of every dollar of the price is profit. The calculator's target rate per paid hour.
